description: Two polyphonic coin tossers, each sending its input signal to one of two outputs on every trigger, with a crossfade so the swap does not click

params.text: Sets the odds of the toss for that section: at the top every trigger sends the signal to A, at the bottom every trigger sends it to B in direct mode or swaps the outputs in toggle mode
Chooses how the toss is read, the panel printing M: Direct sends the signal to A on heads and to B on tails; Toggle leaves it where it is on heads and swaps it over on tails. It comes up in Direct
Sets how long the signal takes to fade from one output to the other after a swap, 0 to 10 seconds; at 0 the crossfader is off and the swap is instant

inputs.text: The signal that section routes to one of its two outputs; the second section's is normalled to the first section's
Shifts the odds for that section; the voltage is divided by 5 and added to the probability slider, and it is read one voltage per channel
A trigger above 2V tosses the coin for that section and chooses an output; the second section's is normalled to the first section's

outputs.text: One of the two destinations for that section's signal; it carries the input while it is selected and silence while it is not, with the crossfade between

notes: Polyphony for a section comes from its signal and trigger inputs, whichever carries more channels; a monophonic probability CV modulates channel 1 only.
The second section's trigger input is normalled to the first section's, so one trigger can drive both halves; the manual mentions only the signal normalling.
A signal is always at one output or the other: a new module, or a freshly loaded patch, sends it to A.
menu: LEDs channel — picks which polyphonic channel the lights on both sections show; only channels the cables carry are listed, and it defaults to channel 1

inputs.1:
bipolar · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the section 1 signal input.
inputs.2:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
inputs.3:
continuous · polyphonic

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
